verdict: Freeport's revenue rose 8% to $7.5B because copper fetched $6.54 a pound — high metal prices more than made up for selling fewer pounds while the Grasberg mine ramps back up.

segments.name: U.S. Rod & Refining
segments.note: Copper rod and cathode sold to outside customers from U.S. conversion plants.

segments.name: South America operations
segments.note: Cerro Verde in Peru and El Abra in Chile — copper sold to outside customers.

segments.name: Indonesia operations
segments.note: The Grasberg district — copper, gold and silver; sales held back by the mine's ramp-up and gold timing.

segments.name: Atlantic Copper
segments.note: Smelting and refining in Spain, selling refined copper and precious metals.

segments.name: Corporate & molybdenum sales
segments.note: Includes the molybdenum sales company (molybdenum from the Colorado mines and copper mines) and other corporate revenue.

segments.name: U.S. Copper Mines
segments.note: Direct sales to outside customers only — most U.S. mine output is sold inside the company to Rod & Refining above.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — head office, finance, legal and HR.

opex.name: Exploration & research
opex.note: Looking for new deposits and mining technology work.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $86M, partly offset by $25M of other income, plus $6M of equity earnings from affiliated companies.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.46 a year ago; adjusted EPS $0.88

takeaways.title: Price beat volume
takeaways.text: Copper sales fell 23% to 749 million pounds as Grasberg ramps up, but the price Freeport got rose 40% to $6.54 a pound — so revenue still grew 8% and operating income rose 19% to $2,353M.

takeaways.title: Gold sales were deferred, not lost
takeaways.text: Gold sales were only 105 thousand ounces against production of 234 thousand, because refined gold sat in inventory at the Indonesian smelter; about 60 thousand ounces shifted into Q4, when Freeport expects 300 thousand ounces of gold sales.

takeaways.title: Costs per pound rose
takeaways.text: Unit net cash costs — what it costs to produce a pound of copper after by-product credits — rose to $2.07 from $1.40 a year ago, on lower volumes and higher energy and other input costs.

oneTimers: Adjusted net income of $1,275M ($0.88 per share) excludes $101M of after-tax charges, mainly $244M of pre-tax idle-facility, recovery and restoration costs from PT Freeport Indonesia's September 2025 mud rush incident (with related depreciation).
Revenue includes a favorable $52M adjustment to earlier provisionally priced copper sales.
footerNote: Mining format: revenue is split by operating division's sales to unaffiliated customers from the release's segment schedule (the divisions mine and sell copper, gold and molybdenum; U.S. mines sell mostly inside the company, so their direct external sales are small). Cost of revenue is total cost of sales (production and delivery $4,479M plus depreciation, depletion and amortization $520M). Net income of $1,688M is the total before $514M attributable to non-controlling interests; $1,174M was attributable to Freeport common stockholders.
